findings.passage: We need to make voting easier, not harder in America. I am in favor of the Freedom to Vote Act, which would expand early voting access , mandate mail-in ballots in every state, implement automatic voter registration as well as same-day voter registration and online voter registration , and make sure that voting lines do not last longer than 30 minutes , among many other protections.
findings.note: From the Protecting Democracy issue page on his campaign site. He backs the Freedom to Vote Act and voting-access changes. He does not mention ID or proof of citizenship on this page. The date is the snapshot date Ballotpedia gives for the campaign site text; the page itself is undated.
subjects: voting access laws (Freedom to Vote Act)

findings.passage: We can safeguard our democracy by removing money from politics and protecting voter rights.
findings.note: Campaign site statement on protecting voter rights. No mention of ID or citizenship checks. Date is Ballotpedia's snapshot date for the site text.

findings.passage: I support an assault weapons ban, universal background checks, and red flag laws.
findings.note: Campaign issue page states his support for an assault weapons ban, universal background checks and red flag laws. Page is undated.

findings.passage: Massachusetts has shown that strong and common-sense gun safety laws save lives, and we need to bring that approach nationwide.
findings.note: Campaign issue page says Massachusetts gun laws should be a national model. Page is undated.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: I was proud that we passed the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act in the Biden Administration, but that was only a first step.
findings.note: Campaign issue page cites the 2022 federal gun law as a first step needing more action. He worked in the administration, not in Congress. Page is undated.
